nodes.title: Stably reflexive module
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R and an R-module M, stable reflexivity means that the native evaluation M→M** is bijective and Ext_R^i(M,R)=Ext_R^i(M*,R)=0 for every i>0, where M*=Hom_R(M,R). The predicate itself imposes no finiteness. The finite Noetherian theory below adds those hypotheses explicitly. On finite modules over a Noetherian R this agrees with the existing finitely generated Gorenstein-projective predicate; no second complete-resolution or Gorenstein-projective object is defined here.
hypotheses: R is commutative; M is an R-module.
proofSteps: Conjoin the existing reflexivity predicate with categorical vanishing of the two actual positive Ext families.
Use native ModuleCat Ext objects; identify their zero objects with vanishing of the underlying module.

In the finite Noetherian case, splice the two finite free resolutions to compare with the imported Gorenstein-projective predicate; in the other direction its totally acyclic complex gives the two Ext vanishings and canonical biduality. This is a compatibility theorem, not a new complete-resolution infrastructure.
acceptance: The bidual map must be canonical evaluation.
Both positive Ext families, at every degree, are required.

The image consists of contractions of maximal ideals of R, not necessarily maximal ideals of A. The predicate imposes no hidden finiteness.

nodes.title: Universally acyclic complete hull
nodes.statement: For Noetherian A,R, a flat map A→R, and finite relatively stably reflexive M, choose the existing StablePeriodicCurved Layer 2 finite-projective complete complex E with augmentation M≃coker(d_E^(-1)) and the additional coefficient-universality property below. Put (E∨)^i=Hom_R(E^(1−i),R) and d_(E∨)^i=(d_E^(−i))*; there is no alternating sign in this shifted-dual convention. Both E⊗_A N and E∨⊗_A N are exact for every A-module N. Every cycle of E and E∨ is finite over R and flat over A. This is an existence theorem with comparison maps, not a preferred resolution functor. Its underlying complex is the imported totally acyclic complex. Because M=coker d^(−1)≃Z¹(E), E shifted by one has the supplier cycle convention M≃Z⁰(E[1]); the shifted dual here is an explicit reindexing of its ordinary dual.
hypotheses: A,R are Noetherian; R is A-flat; M is finite over R and relatively stably reflexive.
proofSteps: Use the imported finite-projective totally acyclic complex and complete-resolution comparison infrastructure. For the relative existence theorem, splice finite free resolutions of M and M* through evaluation; the new content is universal exactness over A and A-flat cycles, not definition of an ordinary complete resolution.
Apply the fibre/coefficient criterion to E and its shifted dual. Exactness after every coefficient tensor makes each short exact sequence of cycles universally exact.
Flatness of the finite projective terms over A and the Tor exact sequences give A-flatness of all cycles; finite generation follows from Noetherianity.
Record the finite-projective dual-tensor isomorphisms before comparing E∨ with the dual of a base-changed complex.
acceptance: Coker degree −1, not a randomly chosen homology group, is M.
All coefficient modules and both complexes must be tested.

nodes.title: Universal coefficient criterion
nodes.statement: For Noetherian A,R, A→R flat, and M finite over R, relative stable reflexivity is equivalent to the following for every A-module N: α_N:M*⊗_A N→Hom_R(M,R⊗_A N), f⊗n↦(m↦f(m)⊗n), and β_N:M⊗_A N→Hom_R(M*,R⊗_A N), m⊗n↦(f↦f(m)⊗n), are isomorphisms, and Ext_R^i(M,R⊗_A N)=Ext_R^i(M*,R⊗_A N)=0 for every i>0. It is also equivalent to existence of a universally acyclic complete hull. In particular M and M* are A-flat and M→M** is canonical evaluation.
hypotheses: Noetherian A,R; R A-flat; M finite over R.
proofSteps: For the fibre definition, use the coefficient cohomology/base-change criterion on finite projective presentations and both resolution complexes; filtered colimits extend finite coefficients to every N.
Identify β_N with canonical bidual evaluation followed by the first Hom exchange for M*.
Conversely the two exchange maps force M* and M to be A-flat by the same coefficient criterion; change-of-rings for their flat fibres gives biduality and both fibre Ext vanishings.
The complete-hull characterization is the splicing theorem and the converse obtained by reading Hom cohomology of the two halves.
acceptance: β_N is evaluation, not an arbitrary isomorphism between modules.

Canonical duals and all coefficient Hom/Ext comparison maps are obtained by tensoring finite free resolutions, not by assuming Hom commutes with an inverse limit.

For each A-module N identify T⊗_R(R⊗_A N) with T⊗_A N.
Flat tensor commutes with homology; faithful flat tensor detects the kernel and cokernel of α_N, β_N and each positive Ext module.

nodes.title: Knudsen completion theorem
nodes.statement: Let (A,p)→(R,m) be a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and M a finite R-module. Write Â=lim A/p^n, R̂=lim R/m^n and M̂=R̂⊗_R M, with the continuous local map Â→R̂. Then R̂ is flat over Â, and the following are equivalent: M is relatively stably reflexive over A; M̂ is relatively stably reflexive over A; M̂ is relatively stably reflexive over Â. These statements use all A-modules and all Â-modules in their respective universal criteria. In each case M̂*=R̂⊗_R M* canonically.
hypotheses: A→R flat and local; A,R Noetherian local; M finite over R; both completions are at the displayed maximal ideals.
proofSteps: Faithfully flat R→R̂ gives equivalence of the first two conditions and identifies the completed dual by finite-presentation flat Hom base change.

Flat A→Â has the same residue field k. For any Â-module B, a free A-resolution of k tensored with Â gives Tor_1^Â(k,B)≃Tor_1^A(k,B). Apply the local Tor criterion to the finite R̂-module B=R̂; its A-flatness proves Â-flatness of R̂.

For the second condition take an A-universally acyclic finite projective R̂-hull. Its cycles and shifted-dual cycles are finite R̂-modules and A-flat. Apply the same Tor comparison and local Tor criterion to each cycle, proving Â-flatness. Their short exact cycle sequences stay exact after tensor with every Â-module, so the hull is Â-universal.
In the reverse direction a hull universal over Â has Â-flat cycles; restricting along the flat A→Â makes its cycles A-flat, hence makes both complexes universal over A.
This supplies the needed completion input by a public local-flatness proof. It does not infer any ordinary tensor/limit interchange for arbitrary completed coefficients.
acceptance: The map Â→R̂ must be the continuous extension of A→R.

nodes.statement: For a flat local map of Noetherian local rings (A,p)→(R,m), finite R-module M and ideal I⊆p, M is relatively stably reflexive over A if and only if M/I^nM is relatively stably reflexive over A/I^n for every n≥1, with chart ring R/I^nR. nodes.title: Completed-ring Hom and Ext
nodes.statement: For a flat map of commutative rings R→T, any R-module L, and any T-module V, restriction along L→T⊗_R L gives canonical Hom_T(T⊗_R L,V)≃Hom_R(L,V), f↦(l↦f(1⊗l)). The derived comparison gives Ext_T^i(T⊗_R L,V)≃Ext_R^i(L,V) for all i≥0, because a projective R-resolution remains a projective T-resolution. Apply this to T=R̂ and L=J or J*. For the parent finite-projective completed coefficients, composing with its compatible-quotient Hom comparison identifies actual completed-ring Hom with those families. This comparison makes no claim that arbitrary Ext commutes with inverse limits.

Apply the Hom adjunction degreewise and pass to cohomology; identify the degree-zero map with the explicit one.

nodes.title: Pointed hull and completed family chart
nodes.statement: Let C→Spec A be a flat finitely presented nodal curve over a Noetherian local ring, with section Δ through a node of its closed fibre, and x=Δ(p). This is the (p,u,v)-adic completion of the parent polynomial model over Â. The isomorphism sends the actual section ideal to (u−s,v−t), and its actual dual and residue quotient to the completed parent ones. Its maps, rather than its coordinate choices, are the data retained in a comparison. At a smooth point the corresponding chart is Â[[z]], Δ(z)=a. No fine representability or canonical hull ring for a stack is asserted.

nodes.title: Section ideal of a local Gorenstein family
nodes.statement: Let (A,p)→(R,m) be a flat local map of Noetherian local rings with a retraction R→A whose composite is the identity, and suppose R/pR is a one-dimensional Gorenstein local ring. For J=ker(R→A), J is relatively stably reflexive over A. Multiplication embeds R in J*=Hom_R(J,R), and J*/R is free of rank one over A, supported on the section. Its generator is a choice, not a canonical trivialization. Duals and this exact quotient commute with arbitrary coefficient base change. In particular this applies at every smooth or nodal point of a section of a Noetherian nodal family.
hypotheses: Local flat Noetherian coefficient map with a specified section retraction; one-dimensional Gorenstein closed chart fibre.
proofSteps: The exact sequence 0→J→R→A→0 makes J A-flat. On the closed fibre its maximal ideal is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over a one-dimensional Gorenstein ring, hence has canonical biduality and both positive dual Ext vanishings.
Apply the relative fibre criterion. The Hom long exact sequence identifies J*/R with Ext_R^1(A,R); fibre duality and coefficient exchange make this an A-free rank-one module locally.
A fibre regular element in the section ideal lifts to a nonzerodivisor, proving multiplication R→J* injective.
Apply the canonical exchanges for arbitrary coefficients and exactness of the A-flat quotient to obtain the base-change exact sequence.
acceptance: Do not claim the family pairing image J·J*=J.
In R=A[x,y]/(xy−bc), Δ(x)=b, Δ(y)=c, the section pullback of J* is A⊕A/(b,c), so the rank-two statement holds only on the persistent nodal-section locus.

nodes.title: Global section dual and residue line
nodes.statement: For a nodal family C/S over a locally Noetherian scheme, an arbitrary section Δ with ideal sheaf J has a quasi-coherent dual J∨=Hom_O_C(J,O_C) and an exact sequence 0→O_C→J∨→Δ_*L_Δ→0, with L_Δ invertible on S. These are the actual sheaf dual and quotient, and their formation commutes canonically with every base change S′→S, including non-Noetherian S′. The canonical Hom comparisons agree on chart overlaps, satisfy identity and composition laws, and coincide with the parent polynomial generators wherever those coordinates are chosen.
hypotheses: C/S flat, finitely presented, nodal of pure relative dimension one; S locally Noetherian; Δ arbitrary.
proofSteps: Use the local Gorenstein theorem at each point on Δ and invertibility of J off Δ. Localize the canonical dual exchange maps on affine charts.
The quotient is annihilated by J and hence is Δ_* of an O_S-module. The local rank-one identifications make that module invertible; they are not a chosen global trivialization.
Glue actual internal Hom modules by their universal property; polynomial formulas give chart comparisons, while uniqueness gives the cocycle.
The local universal coefficient theorem identifies the sheaf pullback dual with the dual of the pulled-back ideal for arbitrary S′; exactness of the quotient is preserved by its coefficient flatness.
acceptance: A residue generator changes by a unit on overlaps and must descend as a line.
Arbitrary base change is justified by relative reflexivity; the generic flat-base-change theorem for internal Hom alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Collision chart of pointed expansion
nodes.statement: In an étale smooth coordinate neighborhood with old marking z=0 and extra section z=a over a commutative ring A, the parent diagonal-cokernel expansion has the actual presentation Proj_(A[z]) A[z][U,V]/((z−a)U+zV), with U,V in degree one. Its U-chart is z(1+v)=a, v=V/U, and its V-chart is z(u+1)=au, u=U/V. The new marking is v=0,z=a, the old one is u=0,z=0. Over a=0 the exceptional P¹ has new mark v=0, old mark v=∞, and attaching point v=−1. The coordinates are local choices; the scheme is the parent intrinsic Proj construction.
hypotheses: A arbitrary commutative ring; the curve is étale locally the smooth coordinate chart; exactly one old mark can meet Δ because old marks are pairwise disjoint.
proofSteps: Trivialize J∨ by 1/(z−a) and O(D) by 1/z; the diagonal map is the column ((z−a),z).
Take the symmetric algebra of this actual cokernel, obtaining the displayed linear homogeneous relation.
Dehomogenize and read the quotient lines defining the lifted sections.
Glue the two charts; changing the generators multiplies the homogeneous coordinates by units, yielding the same intrinsic expansion.
acceptance: The signs must match the parent positive diagonal map.
The three special points on the exceptional line remain distinct in characteristic two.

nodes.title: Flatness at an old-mark collision
nodes.statement: The collision Proj is flat and finitely presented over every coefficient ring A. Its geometric fibres are nodal, its two lifted markings are smooth and disjoint, and the collision fibre has the same arithmetic genus as the original curve. For a=0 the inserted rational tail has exactly the old mark, the new mark and its attachment as special points.
hypotheses: The collision chart and its intrinsic gluing are as specified; no flatness or regularity is imposed on a.
proofSteps: On D_+(U), write w=1+v: the ring A[z,w]/(zw−a) is A-free with the normal-form basis 1,z^i,w^j for i,j≥1.
The rest is covered in D_+(V) by u+1 invertible, where z=au/(u+1) and the ring is A[u,(u+1)^(−1)]. These two opens cover because outside U one has u=0.
At the new and old sections the relative Jacobian in z is a unit; the sections are disjoint since their homogeneous coordinates differ.
Use the fibre union and normalization exact sequence to read nodality and genus, and the three flags to read stability of the tail.
acceptance: The affine cover is displayed and is valid over nonreduced A.
The new marking is not the attaching point; its smoothness is a relative assertion.

nodes.title: Flatness transfer from the pointed formal chart
nodes.statement: For the Noetherian pointed nodal family, C^s=Proj_C Sym K is flat over the coefficient base near the preimage of a nodal section point. The completed family comparison identifies its formal affine charts with completed base changes of the parent polynomial expansion charts. This is a statement about actual local rings of the intrinsic Proj. It uses neither algebraization of an arbitrary formal scheme nor excellence of the coefficient ring.
hypotheses: Noetherian local coefficient base; finitely presented nodal curve with section; the intrinsic finite-presentation sheaf K and the pointed formal comparison.
proofSteps: On a distinguished affine H of the actual Proj over the local chart R, the formal ring is lim H/m^kH, where m is the maximal ideal of R at the section point. This is completion along the inverse image of that point. Use Sym/Proj base change and then complete this affine ring; a polynomial algebra over R̂ is not itself presumed complete.

The pointed formal comparison identifies these rings with the (p,u,v)-adic completions of the parent polynomial expansion charts over Â. The first polynomial chart has monic leading term vy²; the complementary localization of the second is a polynomial localization. Their explicit parent normal forms give Â-flatness before completion.

All these polynomial charts are Noetherian. Their displayed ideal-adic completions are flat over them and hence Â-flat. At a point under test, localize in the compared formal charts and complete once more at its maximal ideal; this yields the same maximal-ideal completion B̂ of the actual Proj local ring B. No ordinary tensor product of power-series rings is used.

The resulting B̂ is Â-flat and hence A-flat. Since B→B̂ is faithfully flat, descend A-flatness to B. Away from the exceptional locus the intrinsic Proj is the original curve. This uses only completions of actual Noetherian rings and requires no algebraization of an arbitrary formal scheme.
acceptance: Distinguish completion after coefficient base change from a bare tensor product with R_pd.
State the ideals of formal completion on each distinguished affine and then localize at the point under test.

nodes.title: Approximation of pointed nodal families
nodes.statement: For every scheme S, a stable pointed family C/S and one arbitrary additional section admit, locally on affine S, a model over a finite-type Z-algebra A₀ with a stable pointed nodal family, its ordered markings and additional section. Any finite collection of family isomorphisms and their equations descends after enlargement of A₀. The actual section ideal, its dual, residue line, diagonal cokernel, symmetric algebra and Proj are canonically the pullbacks of the corresponding Noetherian-model objects. Two models give the same comparisons after a common enlargement. No global qcqs hypothesis is imposed on S.
hypotheses: C/S proper, flat and finitely presented, with pure one-dimensional geometrically connected nodal genus-g fibres; ordered disjoint smooth old markings; log-dual relatively ample; arbitrary Δ.
proofSteps: On an affine base descend the finitely presented curve, all sections and the invertible log-dual line. Use the limit property theorems for properness, flatness, syntomic nodality and disjoint smooth markings, and the parent fibre/ample criteria for genus and stability.

The section ideal pulls back exactly: in 0→J→O_C→Δ_*O_S→0, the quotient is S-flat. Over the Noetherian model J is finitely presented, and its actual dual commutes with every coefficient pullback by the relative theorem.
Pull back the residue line and the finite diagonal-cokernel presentation. Sym and Proj commute with coefficient change by their existing universal properties.

Descend morphisms and equations by the finite-presentation limit theorem; compare two choices after a common enlargement. Glue over affine covers and their refinements using the canonical comparisons.
acceptance: A finite-presentation module can have a dual that fails arbitrary base change in general; the section-ideal theorem is the essential extra input.
Do not replace the infinite graded contraction ring by an unjustified interchange of an infinite limit: use the parent finite Veronese presentation.
A non-qcqs base is handled by local affine constructions and descent.

nodes.title: Expansion over arbitrary schemes
nodes.statement: The existing intrinsic diagonal-cokernel construction defines stable (g,n+1)-pointed expansion over every scheme S for each stable pair (g,n), including old-mark collisions and nodal sections. The result is proper, flat and finitely presented over S, of the same genus, with disjoint smooth lifted markings and positive log-dual degree on every geometric component. Its canonical base-change and pointed-isomorphism comparisons satisfy the identity and composition cocycles. The new section is not required to be smooth or disjoint before expansion.
hypotheses: Stable (g,n)-pointed C/S; 2g−2+n>0; arbitrary extra section Δ.
proofSteps: Work over a Noetherian model. The complement of Δ is unchanged; the smooth disjoint case is an isomorphism, the collision case is the displayed tail chart, and the node case is the formal-transfer chart.

These charts prove flatness, nodality, smoothness/disjointness of lifted marks and the geometric three-flag description. The graph/genus and componentwise degree formulas prove same genus and stability.
Pull back to an arbitrary base using the approximation theorem, then glue across affine charts.
All comparisons arise from the canonical sheaf dual, cokernel, Sym and Proj maps, so their identity and composition laws follow from those universal properties.
acceptance: Include all three fibre types in a single construction.
Retain automorphisms of the original pointed family and naturality on their isomorphisms.

nodes.title: Recovery of a contracted pointed family
nodes.statement: Let Y/S be stable (g,n+1)-pointed, and let q:Y→C be the parent contraction after omitting its last marking, with 2g−2+n>0. Let Δ be the image of the omitted mark. There is a unique pointed isomorphism Y≃C^s over C compatible with q, the lifted old markings and the last marking. It is natural in family isomorphisms and every base change. The only contracted component is the rational three-flag tail or bridge rendered unstable by removal of that one marking; no stable component is contracted.
hypotheses: Parent single-mark contraction with its universal structure-sheaf and base-change properties; stable source and stable retained pair.
proofSteps: Use the parent contraction and componentwise log-dual degrees to classify its exceptional fibre: collision tail, nodal bridge, or none.

Write D for the old divisor on C, D_Y for the retained divisor on Y and l for the last section. The fibrewise tail/bridge calculations and cohomology/base change give q_*O_Y(l−D_Y)≃J∨(−D). The evaluation diagram identifies q_*O_Y(l) with K(−D), not K itself, and gives q^*K(−D)→O_Y(l) surjective. Tensor by q^*O_C(D), or use Proj Sym K(−D)≃Proj Sym K, to obtain the map Y→C^s with the specified quotient lines. Keep the signs compatible with the positive diagonal.

The map preserves all quotient lines and is an isomorphism on geometric fibres, hence is quasi-finite. It is proper because Y is proper over S and C^s is separated over S, and is therefore finite. For a finite map between S-flat finitely presented curves, fibrewise isomorphism makes its structure-sheaf map an isomorphism by Nakayama and coefficient-flatness.
The quotient universal property and the contraction factorization property give uniqueness. Prove over Noetherian models and descend to arbitrary S.
acceptance: Verify the sheaf comparison and the induced evaluation quotient, not only a bijection on geometric points.
Include an omitted marking on a rational bridge and one colliding with an old marking.
Retain the twist K(−D) in the recovery evaluation diagram; its Proj is canonically the same as that of K.

nodes.title: Coherent universal-curve equivalence
nodes.statement: The imported morphisms s:Z̄_(g,n)→M̄_(g,n+1) and c:M̄_(g,n+1)→Z̄_(g,n) form an equivalence of groupoid-valued pseudofunctors over M̄_(g,n) on all schemes. The natural isomorphisms cs≅id and sc≅id are the pointed recovery maps; they commute with pullback, satisfy both triangle identities, and respect reindexing of retained markings. For a family C/S classified by S→M̄_(g,n), the two-fibre product S×_(M̄_(g,n)) M̄_(g,n+1) is canonically the actual curve C. The structural projection is proper flat nodal, and the n old marking loci are actual sections of this universal curve.
hypotheses: g,n≥0, 2g−2+n>0; imported curve-moduli groupoids and their coherent pullback.
proofSteps: Apply the recovery comparison to sc; contracting the intrinsic expansion recovers the original family and its arbitrary extra section, giving cs.
Uniqueness of pointed recovery over the contraction makes the two unit/counit composites agree, proving triangle identities and all pullback squares.
The universal-curve moduli problem represents arbitrary sections of C_T; the equivalence identifies its groupoid with the two-fibre product.
Transport the actual proper flat nodal curve morphism and marking sections through this equivalence.

At a fibre node the projection is nodal, not smooth.

nodes.title: Stable genus-one curves and one-gons
nodes.statement: For every scheme S, forgetting the generalized elliptic action gives an equivalence from the imported one-gon generalized elliptic groupoid E₁(S) to the groupoid of stable one-pointed genus-one curves over S. The inverse uses the unique group law on the relative smooth locus with the mark as identity, and its unique extension action on the cubic. It commutes with arbitrary pullback. Consequently M̄₁,₁ is proper smooth Deligne–Mumford over Z of relative dimension one; its reduced boundary is the smooth Cartier stack B(C₂). This proof is independent of the triangle embedding.
hypotheses: Stable pointed genus-one family; the ordered single mark is relatively smooth.
proofSteps: The total log-dual degree is 2g−2+n=1. Positivity on each geometric component forces one component: a smooth genus-one curve or an irreducible rational nodal curve.

The degree-three marked polarization gives the relative noncuspidal Weierstrass cubic locally on S. Use the existing integral Weierstrass presentation and its coordinate-change group; its generalized elliptic law is uniquely recovered from the pointed cubic.
The coordinate comparisons descend and are compatible with all pullbacks, identifying the two groupoids and preserving their automorphisms.
Import properness, smoothness, DM and the one-gon cusp from the arithmetic-moduli nodes; no new construction of generalized elliptic curves is made here.

The nodal cusp retains the inversion automorphism; it is B(C₂), not Spec Z.

nodes.title: Universal-curve induction
nodes.statement: Suppose for a stable pair (g,n) the imported M̄_(g,n) is smooth proper DM over Z, of relative dimension d=3g−3+n, and its nodal deformations have independent smoothing coordinates with reduced normal-crossings boundary. Then M̄_(g,n+1) has the same properties with dimension d+1. Over a point at an old node, the universal curve replaces its base coordinate t₁ by xy=t₁, so x and y are the two smoothing coordinates of the expanded bridge. Over an old-mark collision its new tail has smoothing coordinate a transverse to the old boundary. This is an induction theorem, not an assertion that the universal projection is smooth.
hypotheses: The stated smooth proper DM and independent-node-coordinate hypotheses for (g,n); 2g−2+n>0.
proofSteps: Representability of the universal-curve morphism transfers DM algebraicity from the base and gives properness by composition; its relative dimension is one.

On a smooth atlas at a point away from an old node, the universal curve is smooth relative dimension one. At an old node its local deformation equation is xy=t₁; eliminating the independent parameter t₁ proves smoothness of the total space over Z.

At a collision, the explicit tail chart identifies the new node parameter with the transverse coordinate a; at an old node the bridge chart identifies its two node parameters with x,y. Retain every other old node coordinate.

Thus the boundary coordinates remain independent, and the complement of their zero loci is the dense smooth-family open. Use the same atlas and the formal-to-étale coordinate comparison already required by MC.1, rather than infer étale normal crossings from arbitrary formal equations.
acceptance: Dimension increases by one, including g=0 and g=1.
The nodal universal projection remains nonsmooth at xy=t₁ with x=y=0.
Prove smoothness and the node-coordinate hypothesis together in the induction.

nodes.title: Boundary under forgetting a mark
nodes.statement: Under the universal-curve equivalence, the reduced boundary divisors satisfy B_(g,n+1)=π*B_(g,n)+Σ_(i=1)^n s_i(M̄_(g,n)) as relative effective Cartier divisors on the universal curve. The first term records old nodal fibres; the extra n section divisors record new old-mark collision tails. At a universal point on the j-th old node, t_j=xy and a local boundary equation becomes xy∏_(k≠j)t_k; at an old marking a local equation is a∏_k t_k. These are normal crossings étale locally, without asserting globally simple normal crossings.
hypotheses: The induction-step hypotheses, and reduced boundary with independent smoothing coordinates; ordered disjoint old markings.
proofSteps: A new expanded family is nodal exactly when the old curve was nodal or the extra point meets an old mark.
The local smoothing calculations give multiplicity one for every component and identify the Cartier equations.
Old markings lie in the smooth locus and are disjoint, so their new divisors are smooth relative to the base and meet only the old boundary branches transversely.
Use the independent coordinates on a smooth atlas to descend relative normal crossings.
acceptance: For (g,n)=(0,3), the old boundary is empty but the new boundary has three components.
Do not omit the section terms or call the global boundary simple.

nodes.title: Recovery of the labelled rational triangle
nodes.statement: Let E/Z be the fixed three-pointed rational triangle of the parent target, and let ι attach its mark P₁ to a stable one-pointed genus-one family F, retaining P₂,P₃. For every scheme S, each isomorphism of the resulting ordered two-pointed genus-two families lifts uniquely to an isomorphism of the original F families and the identity on E_S. Recovery and its comparisons commute with arbitrary base change, including nilpotent thickenings. Hence ι is a representable monomorphism. Using the independent genus-one properness theorem and separatedness of M̄₂,₂, it is a proper monomorphism and therefore a closed immersion.
hypotheses: E is the fixed labelled triangle, not an arbitrary three-pointed genus-one curve; the target retains the ordered P₂,P₃; S arbitrary.
proofSteps: For a glued family identify the three triangle components by their labelled graph and the two retained markings; the attachment is the unique separating edge adjacent to the unmarked triangle vertex. This graph identification is invariant under every pointed isomorphism.

The four persistent nodes are actual sections of the relative singular scheme. For a proper nodal curve this scheme is finite unramified over S. Its open diagonal makes two sections agreeing on all geometric fibres equal even over nilpotent bases. Thus a pointed family isomorphism preserves these four singular sections scheme-theoretically, not just as vertices of fibre graphs.

Cut the four selected nodes by the canonical finite algebra End(I), where I is their ideal. On an étale persistent-node chart R=A[x,y]/(xy), I=(x,y), this algebra is A[x]⊕A[y]; its equal-constant subalgebra is R. The completed version is A[[x]]⊕A[[y]]. Away from the selected sections I is the unit ideal, so End(I)=R. These calculations glue and commute with coefficient change, giving a partial normalization only at the selected nodes. Every isomorphism preserving I lifts canonically to this cut; this is not normalization of the whole nonreduced family.

Each recovered rational component has three labelled disjoint smooth sections, so the imported genus-zero base identifies it uniquely with P¹; thus its automorphism is the identity. The remaining component with its recovered attachment mark is F.
Glue the local recovery maps uniquely by the pushout property and descend from Noetherian models; this proves full faithfulness over arbitrary S, not only on geometric points.

A monomorphism of these algebraic stacks is representable. Properness of the source over Z and separatedness of the ambient target make this map proper; a proper representable monomorphism is a closed immersion.

Include nonreduced bases; fibre graph uniqueness by itself is insufficient.

nodes.title: Four fixed triangle smoothing parameters
nodes.statement: At a geometric point in the labelled triangle immersion, choose the independent ambient M̄₂,₂ node-smoothing coordinates. Its formal image is defined by the vanishing of the four coordinates for the three internal triangle nodes and the attachment. The remaining parameter is free. If F is nodal, it is precisely its fifth ambient node-smoothing parameter and cuts out the boundary of M̄₁,₁; if F is smooth it is the one-dimensional smooth deformation coordinate. After the MC.1 formal-to-étale comparison these equations describe the image étale locally. There is no assertion that the fifth parameter vanishes on the whole image.
hypotheses: Geometric pointed triangle point; specified branches of the four persistent nodes; independent ambient node parameters on a smooth atlas.
proofSteps: The three rational triangle components have three labelled flags each and thus no moduli; retain their four gluing nodes unsmoothed.
Cutting those nodes as in the family-recovery theorem identifies their equisingular deformation groupoid with the one-pointed genus-one deformation groupoid.
The ambient independent-node deformation ring therefore restricts by setting exactly those four parameters to zero; the source dimension one accounts for the remaining coordinate.
At a nodal F its own self-node is left free, so its parameter is the source cusp parameter. Apply the same formal-to-étale supplier as the ambient boundary theorem.
acceptance: The ambient relative dimension is five and the source relative dimension is one.
At nodal F count five nodes, of which exactly four are fixed.
